target_customer: Small and mid-sized subscription businesses (eLearning, SaaS, membership, magazines, gyms) that pay for billing and revenue management software
problem: SMBs with subscriptions struggle to bill, track churn risk and cross-sell; SubscriptionFlow offers customizable billing with AI alerts for at-risk customers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for billing and revenue management

founders.name: Kashif Saleem
education: Certified in Technology Entrepreneurship, London Business School
founders.background_notes: YC page: over 12 years helping SMBs with SaaS apps, cloud computing research fellow at Oxford, high-frequency programmer in London equity trading at JP Morgan Chase.

competitors.name: Chargebee
competitors.what: Subscription billing and revenue management platform
competitors.traction_then: Not found with a dated source

competitors.name: Recurly
competitors.traction_then: Not found with a dated source

competitors.name: Zuora
competitors.traction_then: Not found with a dated source

technical_complexity.rationale: Billing, plan management and payment gateway integrations are standard SaaS engineering; the AI churn alerts add modest data work.

defensibility.rationale: Billing data and integrations create some lock-in, but well-funded incumbents like Chargebee and Recurly offer overlapping features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established billing vendors already served SMBs; no copy or acquisition event was found, and SubscriptionFlow stayed small.

market_need_then: The subscription economy was growing and SMBs needed billing and churn tools; the company site gives examples such as eLearning, SaaS and membership. No independent demand data was opened.

branding.domain_note: Uses subscriptionflow.com, the exact compound of the name.

identity.logo: Full-color logo with icon seen on the HubSpot marketplace listing
identity.visual_style: Standard B2B SaaS marketing site with comparison blog posts

branding.community_and_virality: Capterra shows 4.7 on 35 reviews and G2 4.6 on 33 reviews per search snippets; no press about the brand itself found.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name close to category terms, modest review counts and no independent brand coverage.

outcome_analysis: SubscriptionFlow is still active as a small company but shows no confirmed outside round after YC W22. It entered a market with established billing vendors, and self-reported estimates suggest revenue near 1.5M in 2025, down from 2.4M in 2024. It adds AI features, yet no breakout growth is documented.
notes: No funding round recorded. CB Insights lists a 500K convertible note dated 2022-03-29 (investor shown as Y Combinator or Lombardstreet Ventures depending on source), which matches the size of YC's standard deal, so it is not recorded as a round. Latka estimates (revenue 2.4M in 2024, 1.5M in 2025, 14 employees) are self-reported and unverified. Founding year conflicts: 2017 Latka, 2019 CB Insights, 2021 YC page; company blog says product soft-launched early 2022. Competitor sources are undated comparison pages, so source_date is null and they may postdate the batch. Failure factors are tentative given no shutdown.
